text:
alex: heads-up — got alerts for a few preemptible GPU nodes in us-west-2 that got termination notices. cluster-autoscaler didn't replace capacity quickly because a bunch of gpu jobs were stuck in Terminating. can we look into TTL/controller + node lifecycle hooks? :grimacing:

maria: that's been noisy today. logs show pods stuck because of local-ssd volumes and a long finalizer from our metrics sidecar.

samir: here's the snapshot I pulled: ```
$ kubectl get pods -n ml -o wide | grep Terminating
resnet-train-5k8t  1/1  Terminating  0  12m  ip-10-0-...  node/preemptible-gpu-1
```
They don't move to another node because CA considers the node not fully deletable (local storage). CA then doesn't scale up fallback fast enough.

kevin: two quick levers:
- run node-termination-handler to cordon/drain on notice (gives us the 2m AWS spot notice) and trigger graceful evict
- set CA flags so it can skip nodes with local storage when deciding replacements, and enable balance-similar-node-groups

alex: can you share exact CA flags you'd change? also how does ttl-controller tie in here?

kevin: CA flags I'm thinking:
--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false  # allow CA to consider replacing nodes even if they have local storage
--balance-similar-node-groups=true
--expander=priority

the ttl-controller part: we have batch jobs and ephemeral pods that should be auto-cleaned after they enter Terminating/Failed. currently ttl-after-finished is only for Completed jobs. For stuck Terminating pods we can add a controller that force-deletes pods older than X minutes that have been Terminating > 60s and carry a special label (e.g., preemptible=true)

maria: i'm wary of force-deleting without addressing finalizers. If we delete, kubelet might be mid-unmount and write corruption risk for local-disk. but for GPU training jobs we prefer restart on replacement capacity rather than waiting forever.

samir: compromise: add a controller that only force-deletes if node has a termination notice AND pod has been Terminating > 90s AND pod doesn't have block-storage mounts or has an annotation allow-fast-evict=true. That keeps safety for local-disk-backed stuff.

alex: sounds good. infra-bot posted termination notices earlier in the hour. @infra-bot could you dump the last 2 notices for this ASG?

infra-bot: auto: termination-notice dump for asg/gpu-preemptible-usw2
- i-0a1b2c3d4e5f  notice at 1769009900  action: ENI detach scheduled
- i-0f9e8d7c6b5a  notice at 1769010200  action: instance-terminate

kevin: implementation plan:
1) deploy/aws node-termination-handler as DaemonSet (handles SIG for both AWS/GCP)
   kubectl apply -f https://github.com/aws/aws-node-termination-handler/releases/latest/deploy/kubernetes/daemonset.yaml
2) add a lightweight TTL-for-Terminating controller (k8s job) — policy:
   - label selector: preemptible=true
   - condition: pod.Status==Terminating && age>90s && node.terminationNotice==true && no-block-storage
   - action: kubectl delete pod --grace-period=30 --force
3) change CA flags (update helm values for cluster-autoscaler):
   args:
   - --skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false
   - --balance-similar-node-groups=true
   - --expander=least-waste
4) test on staging ASG with mixed pools (spot + on-demand) and run a churn test

maria: i can wire up the TTL controller skeleton. need a small RBAC service account and a configmap for the policy (so ops can tune age/grace-period).

samir: i'll own the CA helm change and run trials in staging. will monitor scale-up latency metric: ca.replacement.latency

alex: safety checks: add a global PDB for critical controllers so we don't evict all replicas simultaneously. also add a feature-flagged rollout for 24 hours in staging, then prod canary.

kevin: +1. also let's add a log line in the TTL controller so SLO on forced-evictions can be audited (pod, node, reason, age).

maria: noted. i'll add annotation "forced-evict=true" on deletions for auditing.

alex: timeline? maria & samir will pair tomorrow morning, deploy to staging, run a 2-hour preemption simulation. kevin will verify CA behavior. if green, we roll to prod next Tues with canary.

samir: filing a quick runbook update and a follow-up incident alerting rule: if ca.replacement.latency > 90s for >5m, page infra oncall.

kevin: also worth a cost note — if we accept slightly more on-demand fallback while spot churn is high, it's a tiny bump in cost but big win for reliability. will include numbers in the rollout PR.

alex: ok, thanks. tagging @oncall to keep an eye on us-west during the rollout. :thumbsup:
